---
title: "gnafr: Fast Australian Address Matching"
---

[`gnafr`](https://github.com/KyleHaynes/anthropic_address/tree/main/gnafr) is an R
package for fuzzy-matching messy, free-text address strings against the
[Geocoded National Address File (GNAF)](https://geoscape.com.au/data/g-naf/) —
Australia's authoritative address dataset. It's built for bulk workloads
(100k+ addresses in a single call), backed by an embedded [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/)
database, with a transparent 0–100 confidence score per match.

- **Bulk matching** — vectorised, scores entirely inside DuckDB
- **Fuzzy matching** — handles abbreviations, typos, missing fields, messy real-world strings
- **Confidence scoring** — postcode, suburb, street name/type, number and flat all scored independently
- **Custom addresses** — add your own records and match against them alongside GNAF
- **Primary/secondary & alias awareness** — distinguishes a main dwelling from its sub-dwellings, and alias addresses from their principal record

This page is a short, self-contained walkthrough using a handful of made-up
records — it isn't connected to a live database, so you can read it without
downloading anything. See the
[README](https://github.com/KyleHaynes/anthropic_address/tree/main/gnafr) for
full installation and usage instructions.

## Installation

```r
install.packages(c("data.table", "DBI", "duckdb", "stringdist"))
devtools::install_local("gnafr")
```

## A minimal example

GNAF Core ships as a CSV with one row per address. For this walkthrough,
here's a tiny made-up dataset in that format — four addresses on two
fictional streets in "Sampleton QLD". Note the two units at 12 Example
Street: each is flagged `SECONDARY` and points back to its parent record via
`PRIMARY_PID`, which is exactly how GNAF distinguishes a main dwelling from
its sub-dwellings.

```r
library(data.table)

dummy_gnaf <- data.table(
  ADDRESS_DETAIL_PID = c("GA_DUMMY_0001", "GA_DUMMY_0002", "GA_DUMMY_0003", "GA_DUMMY_0004"),
  ADDRESS_LABEL       = c("10 EXAMPLE STREET, SAMPLETON QLD 4999",
                          "12 EXAMPLE STREET, SAMPLETON QLD 4999",
                          "UNIT 1 12 EXAMPLE STREET, SAMPLETON QLD 4999",
                          "5 DEMO COURT, SAMPLETON QLD 4999"),
  FLAT_TYPE           = c(NA, NA, "UNIT", NA),
  FLAT_NUMBER         = c(NA, NA, "1", NA),
  NUMBER_FIRST        = c(10, 12, 12, 5),
  STREET_NAME         = c("EXAMPLE", "EXAMPLE", "EXAMPLE", "DEMO"),
  STREET_TYPE         = c("STREET", "STREET", "STREET", "COURT"),
  LOCALITY_NAME       = "SAMPLETON",
  STATE               = "QLD",
  POSTCODE            = 4999,
  PRIMARY_SECONDARY   = c("PRIMARY", "PRIMARY", "SECONDARY", "PRIMARY"),
  PRIMARY_PID         = c(NA, NA, "GA_DUMMY_0002", NA),
  LONGITUDE           = c(152.001, 152.002, 152.002, 152.010),
  LATITUDE            = c(-27.001, -27.002, -27.002, -27.010)
)

fwrite(dummy_gnaf, "dummy_gnaf_core.csv")
```

Load it into a fresh `gnafr` database the same way you would a real GNAF
Core download — `gnaf_load()` reads the CSV directly with DuckDB, so it
never has to be pulled into R memory:

```r
library(gnafr)

con <- gnaf_connect(":memory:")
gnaf_init(con)
gnaf_load(con, "dummy_gnaf_core.csv")
#> Loading: dummy_gnaf_core.csv
#> Done: dummy_gnaf_core.csv
#> Total GNAF addresses in database: 4
```

Now match a messy, free-text input against it:

```r
gnaf_match(
  c("unit 1 12 example st sampleton 4999", "10 example street sampleton qld 4999"),
  con,
  max_results = 1
)
```

```
 input_id                          input_raw match_rank total_score                                   address_label primary_secondary   primary_pid
        1 unit 1 12 example st sampleton 4999          1          96   UNIT 1 12 EXAMPLE STREET, SAMPLETON QLD 4999         SECONDARY GA_DUMMY_0002
        2 10 example street sampleton qld 4999         1         100      10 EXAMPLE STREET, SAMPLETON QLD 4999            PRIMARY              NA
```

Despite the input dropping "QLD", abbreviating "STREET" to "ST", and missing
the comma, both rows still resolve to the right record — and the result
carries `primary_secondary` / `primary_pid` straight through, so you can tell
at a glance that the first match is a sub-dwelling of `GA_DUMMY_0002` without
a second lookup.

## Adding your own addresses

Records that aren't in GNAF (a new development, a PO box, an internal site
code) can be added to a separate `custom_addresses` table and are matched
against transparently alongside GNAF:

```r
gnaf_add(con, data.table(
  number_first  = 7,
  street_name   = "DEMO",
  street_type   = "COURT",
  locality_name = "SAMPLETON",
  state         = "QLD",
  postcode      = 4999
))

gnaf_match("7 demo court sampleton qld 4999", con, max_results = 1)
```
